inputs.input: I squeeze into the den mouth and step carefully down into the dark, staff raised, feeling my way a few paces at a time.
I keep moving slowly down the sloping tunnel toward the growl, staff forward, ready to cast Arcane Bolt the moment I can see the hound.
I hold still and listen hard, trying to pin down exactly where the big hound is before it moves.
I cast Arcane Bolt at the big hound's breathing, ahead-right against the slab it's backed against.
I turn and climb back up the sloping tunnel toward the den mouth, listening behind me in case the last hound circles back.
I walk south across the barrow field toward Ashenwell to turn in the completed hound cull at the Guild hall.
I walk the road south and east toward Marrowgate, and once I reach the Guild hall there, I turn in the completed Cull the Barrow Gutter-Hounds contract.
I step into the Guild hall and turn in the completed Cull the Barrow Gutter-Hounds contract at the front desk.
"Cull contract, finished — six hounds down." I hand the clerk the slip with the READY seal.
I knock at the inn door and ask if there's any corner, bench or barn space to sleep for the night, since I'll set out for the next Guild branch in the morning.
"The sweep for hay suits me fine." I take the stable broom, sweep it out, then settle into the barn hay and sleep until morning.
I thank the innkeeper, shoulder my pack, and set out south along the road toward the next Guild branch town.

A group is always reported as creature.new with its count: whether a large passive group of skittish animals is background (one fact) or individual combatants is the engine's decision (src/v4/world.js), not the extractor's. A Guild contract's quest.detail keeps the story; its status, payout, XP and rank are the engine's (the run stored "Contract registered and active; payout 60 cp" while the contract was still on the board). delta-0.94 (Patch 7, dungeon foundations): passage, a way between two rooms of a place explored room by room (a door, a stair, a secret passage) with what stands in it; object.new in, the container feature a thing lies in (a locked chest). delta-0.95 (review of Patch 7): dungeon, a true Dungeon as the world establishes it or someone tells of it (theme, Rank range, a level's Rank, who controls access; how: seen, guild, hidden, rumor). Not every cave or ruin is a Dungeon; its Rank is the world's, never fitted to Alaric. delta-1.1 (Patch 9C-2b): object.new and an offer line carry teaches, what a Skill Stone or a manual teaches as the reply establishes it ({source, fn, tags, aspects}, null for what it does not say); the engine fixes the source's profile from it once (src/v4/items.js skillSource). An ordinary stone, a return stone or a storybook teaches nothing.
rules: Report only what THIS reply establishes, in the order it happens (seq 1, 2, 3 …). Invent nothing.

Alaric's own decisions are in PLAYER ACTIONS and already booked by the engine; never report them as deltas (no payment, purchase, acceptance, turn-in, pick-up of his), and never a fact about what he did (no fact with s "pc" for what he ate, hunted, bought, used or left), nor about his HP, gear, life or death, or a fighter's life or death: the engine keeps those.

Overreach is only for meaningful voluntary PC commitments the narrator invented: paying/buying, accepting/turning in/registering, setting off for a new destination, attacking, giving away/dropping his property, eating or using up his food or things, hunting or killing game he had not chosen to hunt, or Alaric himself picking up/taking something he had not chosen to take. Ordinary world causality is not overreach: NPCs may give Alaric items, help him, refuse him, accompany him, leave, reveal information, create witnesses or otherwise act for their own reasons. Record those world changes normally. What the PLAYER MESSAGE has him say or do himself (his words, a gesture, signing, sitting down) is his own, never overreach; but coin, goods, contracts, registration and journeys change only as PLAYER ACTIONS book them: a payment, purchase, pick-up, acceptance, turn-in, registration or journey that the reply shows, that PLAYER ACTIONS do not book and the CATALOG does not show as done already, is overreach, even when the PLAYER MESSAGE has him do it. The natural steps of an action PLAYER ACTIONS booked are part of that action, never overreach: registering includes signing, the measuring stone and coming back to the counter; a purchase includes carrying it off; a journey includes the road.
Answer every key of expected; each key asks about the PLAYER ACTION with the same number.

Known places, people, quests and objects by their id from the CATALOG; a new place as {"new": {"name", "kind", "parent"}} (parent: a place id or one more {"new": …}). parent is where the place actually lies, never simply where Alaric came from: a place reached by travelling out of a settlement (a waystation or inn on the road, a ford, a camp in the wilds, another village or town) lies in the realm or region (its id when the CATALOG lists it), and a place inside a settlement he has reached lies in that settlement. parent null means inside the place where he is now.

Prices and coin are integers in copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper); with each amount give "said": the reply's own words for it, copied ("two silver", "twelve coppers"), and the engine reads the number from them. The Guild's contract payout and its registration fee are the engine's; report the story's words about them only as facts.
Official Guild contracts come only from the engine's BOARD; never report a new one (if the reply shows one the BOARD lacks: overreach guild_listing).

During the reply that FIRST SHOWS the just-generated official BOARD, every listed quest is still available. Do not claim it was already taken or emit listing.gone in that SAME reading reply. Later, causally established world changes may remove an ignored listing.
A price someone merely mentions is a fact; an offer is a price for something Alaric could buy now.

A person learns Alaric's name only from diegetic evidence: Alaric explicitly says it where they hear him, or visibly writes/shows it where the reply establishes they read it. Third-person narration merely calling the protagonist "Alaric" or "Alaric Red" is never evidence that an NPC learned his name.

Tracks, spoor, hair, a wallow, sounds, shadows or other evidence of an unseen/unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new. Report the evidence as a fact or thread. Use creature.new only when the reply establishes the creature itself as an actual individual/group; keep its in-world species name and choose the separate nearest mechanical anchor.

For a known Guild contract, quest.detail may freely store operational story information such as contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered requirements or plausible verification. It may never alter or restate the engine-owned payout, Guild rank, Quest XP, formal status (registered, active, completed, turned in) or promotion mechanics: those clauses are dropped.

Range Bands use Core #12 only: ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach; SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED; MEDIUM = two; LONG = three. Convert an exact narrated distance once to the most reasonable band. A person about forty yards ahead is not ENGAGED. Preserve an established band unless the reply clearly changes distance; threat/intensity alone never changes a band.

During ACTIVE combat, do not turn the engine's ordinary move away/retreat into intent:flee. A combatant moving SHORT→MEDIUM or MEDIUM→LONG is still in the encounter. Emit intent:flee only when the reply independently establishes that the NPC actually chooses/tries to leave the fight or scene; words that merely describe gaining distance, backing off, retreating one band or keeping away are not enough.
When PLAYER ACTIONS already grant or create a Guild plate, contract slip or other object, do not emit object.new for the narrated hand-over or description of that same booked object.

The engine's automatic loot at the end of a fight (LOOT in the engine block: pelts, fangs, scales, gear, coin) is already in Alaric's pack: never emit object.new, object.move or coin.gift for it, nor for anything else taken from those remains.

For person.new, name:null means the reply did not establish a proper name. Never infer a proper name from the ref token, a nearby place/business title, or capitalization; keep the person anonymous until the story actually names them. When the story later names such a known person, report person.named {who: their id, name}, never a second person.new for them.

For person.new, role is a short plain word for what the person is in the world (bandit, guard, soldier, mage, hunter, merchant, farmer, innkeeper, adventurer), as this reply or the CATALOG's facts establish it, not where they sit or what they do now: people the story shows living from robbery (robbing travellers or carts, keeping stolen loads, planning the next hold-up) are bandit even when it never says the word; a trained town watch or soldier is guard; a spellcaster who fights is mage. Where the story establishes no such role, describe them plainly (camp man, villager): a hidden camp, a weapon, hostility or Alaric's own attack alone make no one a bandit or a trained fighter. When the story later establishes what a known person is, report fact {s: their id, p: "occupation", o: that plain role}.

For person.new, armed is the weapon the person holds ready to fight with as this reply shows it (a drawn sword, a knife in hand or at the belt, a bow in hand or on the back), in a few words ("short sword", "belt knife"); null when they hold none: a weapon only mentioned, stored, lying nearby or being worked on (whetted, mended, cleaned) is not armed. When a known person later draws or takes up a weapon, report fact {s: their id, p: "armed", o: the weapon}.

For person.new, relevant:true means important to Alaric's decision IN THIS SCENE (including captives, clients, bystanders in immediate danger, conversation partners or adversaries). This is not the same as being hostile. Set threat:true ONLY for a visible person already clearly established as an adversary, attacker or immediate armed threat in the fiction; captives, hostages, helpers and neutral conversation partners are threat:false, regardless of relevance. Threat marks tactical opposition for a possible fight, not a decision by that person to attack. Incidental passers-by remain relevant:false. Supply a Range Band for visible relevant people.

Co-presence is not awareness. Use aware only when THIS reply actually establishes whether a present person noticed Alaric: aware when they visibly notice/react to or directly interact with him; unaware when the reply explicitly establishes that they have not noticed him; suspicious when they notice signs but not Alaric himself. If the reply does not establish this, omit aware. Never mark someone aware merely because person.new/position made them present in the same scene.

For creature.new, species is the creature's actual in-world name/type from the reply and may be newly invented fantasy fauna. Separately choose anchor as the nearest ecological/mechanical F1 body-plan from the allowed anchor enum. Do not force the creative species name to equal an anchor. Example: a low plated badger-lizard-like wallow beast may be species:"plated wallow beast", anchor:"armored_beast".

creature.new threat: false marks a creature the reply shows as no foe of Alaric: a pack or riding animal, a draught animal, livestock, a pet, harmless game grazing or fleeing. Leave it null for wild beasts and monsters that are or may be hostile (wolves, rats, boars, spiders, goblins), however timid or wary their kind. A creature marked threat: false is not swept into a fight by an area attack; a deliberate attack on it still makes it a target.

creature.new stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual (or each of the group) as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (half again the size of the others, the heaviest bull of the herd); the engine then fixes its stronger numbers once. Never from a name or label alone ("big boar" said in passing), never for anger, wounds or drama; otherwise null. Elite and Boss are never inferred.

When creatures become visible in the scene, report creature.new immediately (one entry per kind of creature, count for a group), so their canonical target handles, HP and Range are locked before the player chooses to attack. The engine keeps a large passive flock or herd as one background fact; an animal the story later singles out, threatens or attacks is a creature.new of its own.

When PLAYER ACTIONS contains a GATHERS activity and the reply establishes a concrete amount actually gathered for an active Quest GATHER objective, emit object.new for the amount gained THIS reply: kind:"resource", holder:"pc", for_quest:<that quest id>, name matching the objective/proof resource, qty the amount gained, unit matching the objective/proof. A progress fact alone is not enough. Do not emit resources the reply did not say were gathered.

Guild contract proof/verification is narrative guidance, not an exact inventory-string gate. Store the expected verification so the narrator remembers what the job is about, but alternative credible in-world evidence may satisfy the fiction.

For every active Guild contract in the CATALOG, compare THIS reply with its desired end state before answering. When THIS reply clearly establishes that desired end state as substantively achieved, you MUST emit quest.ready even if you also emit arrive, fact, quest.progress or memory; do not leave a clearly achieved contract outcome only as a fact or memory. Partial progress, merely finding a clue, traveling to the site, or planning the next step is not enough. quest.ready does not complete or pay the quest; the player must still explicitly turn it in at a Guild hall.

An escort contract (ESCORT) is achieved only by escorting: Alaric travelled with the escorted people or cargo along the way. Their safe arrival while he waited elsewhere is no quest.ready; an arrangement the client explicitly agreed to instead (guarding the gate) goes into quest.ready alternative.

A known object voluntarily handed to Alaric by an NPC is object.move to:"pc", even if Alaric only asked for it and did not issue a TAKE command. For a newly introduced gift, emit object.new with the giver/NPC as holder and then object.move to:"pc". These are NPC/world agency, not overreach. An unattended object lying in the world still requires Alaric's own TAKE if he picks it up. A thing someone sets out for Alaric to take (puts it on the counter or table for him, pushes it toward him, leaves it by the door for him) and does not keep hold of lies at the place: object.new with holder "here" (or object.move to "here" for a known one); it stays with that person only while they keep hold of it or keep it back.

arrive is where Alaric physically is when the reply ends, or a place the reply has him stop at. A place that only comes into view, that he sees from a distance, passes, skirts or avoids on the way is no arrival; when the reply leaves him on the road between places, report no arrive (or the realm's id when the story plainly leaves him out in the open).

arrive.forced_by is only for an external event that actually relocates Alaric against or independently of his voluntary travel choice (for example arrest, being carried, a collapsing floor, abduction). Do not use it to invent ordinary voluntary travel.

When Alaric arrives somewhere together with people (a client he escorts, a driver, a guide, companions), list their ids from PRESENT in arrive.with, or in the with of the expected go answer. The same for a step into a part of the place he is in or back out of it (a den, a back room, the yard behind): whoever of PRESENT is there with him afterwards (the creatures in the den he walks into, the people he joins inside) goes in with. Whoever is not listed stayed behind at the old place.
Soft continuity deltas are memory, not mechanics. Prefer recording the durable fact once over splitting ordinary fiction into several redundant deltas.
Only the delta types listed below exist. A new place comes into being only through the place ref of an arrive (or the at of a person.new) as {"new": …}; there is no delta for a place alone.

Prices have a direction. offer: someone would SELL Alaric goods or a service (he pays). bid: someone would BUY things Alaric holds (he is paid), with his OBJECTS ids and quantities and one price for all of them. A trader appraising and pricing Alaric's goods ("eight silver for the lot") is a bid, never an offer, and never a new object for "the lot".

Things Alaric takes out, lays out, shows or puts on a counter for someone to look at, appraise or price stay his: no object.move for them, even when the trader handles or weighs them. They change hands only by a sale or a give in PLAYER ACTIONS.

THREADS lists the open story threads: update or resolve one by its id; report a new thread only for a new matter. A place someone tells of, a map shows or a rumour names, and that Alaric has not been to, is place.reported (its details stay the report's), not a fact. When Alaric reaches a place he set off for (the GO's place id), that id is where he arrived, however the reply describes it.

GROUP REFS (hostile, intent, aware, position): one creature by its own handle from PRESENT, never its group's ref. A group's ref ('group …', "the wolves") needs scope "all" (every one of them does it; evidence: the reply's words for that, copied) or "part" (some, not said which: none is booked); without scope it commits no one.

When a person in this reply clearly commits to teaching Alaric a technique (they agree to teach him, a lesson is arranged or begins), report fact {s: their id, p: "teaches", o: "Alaric"}. Alaric asking, a maybe, a price named, a refusal or a demonstration for others is no such fact; whether he learns anything is the engine's (it books lessons and Skills).

A Skill Stone or a manual Alaric finds, is given or could buy: report it as object.new (or an offer line) with teaches as the reply establishes it. Using, activating, studying or reading it is his own action, never a delta: whether he learns anything, and what, is the engine's (it books Skills and progress).

A reported intermediate stop on an authorized GO is arrive at the actual stop, even when expected.arrived is false for the final destination. Never infer an arrival from scene alone or from elapsed time. Use expected.with/arrive.with for companions. The final destination retains its existing id; do not wrap routes or companions into a new destination name.

For quest.ready/progress/close that relies on other changes in THIS answer, depends_on lists their earlier seq numbers as strings (for example ["2","4"]). Cite actual discoveries, observations, handovers or diegetic information, not a rejected actor/arrival or a plan. Discovery/information need no arbitrary working-time requirement. Seeing a missing person may satisfy finding them, never rescuing them. A report is judged against the actual quest goal, not its title alone.

PERSON CONTINUITY: preserve known identities and their established history, including earlier rescues. person.new introduces a new person, never resets a known absent person. A known person actually returning now uses enter with the existing id; autonomous arrivals need no Alaric GO. A new predicament after a rescue needs a new cause in the story, not an unexplained replay of the old incident. For a fuller known name use person.named with the existing id. If a newly introduced fuller name could extend a known name, use distinct_from:that existing id ONLY if the story explicitly establishes a different individual; never infer sameness or difference from similar names alone. Do not persist dependent claims from a contradictory reintroduction.

FREE HELP: NPC requests, help, agreements and offered wages are ordinary facts, promises, threads and memories. Never create private quests or job ids. Formal quest deltas concern only existing Guild contracts. Helping earns no automatic Quest XP or payout.

coin.gift is an ACTUAL new handover now, including voluntary thanks, wages, advance or reward from any present NPC. No job or acceptance is required. Promises and conditional/future payments are facts/threads, not coin.gift. In said quote the exact current handover clause INCLUDING the amount and currency, never invent an amount. For a recount of a RECENT COIN HANDOVER set repeat_of to its existing id; it never pays twice. A distinct new gift uses repeat_of:null even for the same giver/amount.

go.summary: did he arrive, where, and who came with him; arrived is true only when the reply ends with him at the place (seeing it ahead or passing it is false); evaluate Alaric's final location at the END of this reply: when he enters the first interior or mouth tunnel of a Dungeon and remains there, mark arrived:true even if his deeper destination remains ahead, with at set to the actual interior as a known place or {new:{name,kind:'interior',parent:Dungeon id}}; arrived:false if he only sees inside, another actor crosses, the alleged crossing is quoted, hypothetical, in the past or interrupted, or Alaric returned outside. Passing a place without staying there is not arrival. A real intermediate stop can be arrive even while arrived:false for the end goal; seeing the end goal ahead alone is still false.

shape.with: ids of the people who arrived with him, or null

activity.summary: how long it took, and whether he finished

buy.summary: did someone name a price; did the reply show Alaric take, use, consume or pay for it before he himself agreed to that price (a nod or consent the reply invents for him is no agreement)

pay.summary: did someone name the amount; did the reply show Alaric pay before he himself agreed to it (a nod or consent the reply invents for him is no agreement)

sell.summary: did a buyer take it and pay, and how much

deltas.summary: story time that passed

Alaric arrives somewhere after his own GO/roaming action, or because the reply explicitly establishes an external involuntary cause in forced_by; with: the ids of the people who travel and arrive together with him (null when he arrives without anyone)

a person the reply introduces; name only a proper name, else null; present: here with Alaric now; relevant:true for a person important to the current scene (hostage, client, opponent); threat:true ONLY for an actually established opponent or imminent threat, NEVER for a captive or neutral NPC; role: a plain word for what they are (bandit, guard, mage, merchant) when established; armed: the weapon they hold ready, else null; at: where they are if not here; distinct_from: existing person id only when this is explicitly a DIFFERENT person whose fuller name could otherwise extend that identity, else null
the reply says the proper name of a person already known (in PRESENT or the CATALOG) who had no name so far

creatures the reply itself establishes as actual creatures; species is the in-world/display species name, anchor is the nearest F1 mechanical body-plan; never tracks/spoor/hair/sounds alone; count > 1 makes separate creatures; band is current distance; cluster: one short word ("vein") only when the reply shows them packed close together, within a stride or two of each other, else null (a group may stand spread out); stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (never a name alone), else null; threat: false only for a creature the reply shows as no foe (a pack or riding animal, livestock, a pet, harmless grazing game), else null; a group in PRESENT ('group ...') is named by that name as ref: more false = the group named again, more true = newcomers who join it; under a ref of their own, more true = another group or a lone newcomer, false = those of this kind in PRESENT again; null when none of this kind is in PRESENT
a known person comes into the scene
a person leaves or stays behind
a lasting world fact (not about what Alaric holds, pays or has decided)
what a person now knows
a real change in how someone regards Alaric
a moment people will remember

a physical thing the reply establishes; for a new NPC gift create it with the NPC as holder, then object.move it to "pc"; Alaric directly holds a newly introduced object only after his TAKE/GATHER; loose coin is never an object (coin Alaric gains is coin.gift); in: the FEATURES id or name of the container it lies in (a locked chest), else null; effect: heal / restore_mp / restore_sta only for a potion or tonic the reply shows restoring HP / MP / STA, else null (the engine sets how much); teaches: only for a Skill Stone or a manual/primer the reply establishes as teaching a technique, what it teaches as the reply states it (null otherwise; never guessed)
someone/something moves a known object; NPC -> Alaric is allowed as ordinary world agency; never move Alaric's property away from him unless his own action or coercion authorizes it
an object gets a mark ("signed by the waystation master")

thread.t7.1.text: The marsh boar lairs in the reed beds south of the landing; the fishers ask whether Alaric will go into the reeds after it or wait for it to come to him
thread.t7.1.resolution: Alaric's Arcane Bolt killed the boar at the gap's edge.

thread.t18.1.text: More owlbeak rooks are somewhere above the crags, out of sight behind the rock
thread.t18.1.resolution: the unseen birds came off their perches and joined the fight

thread.t25.1.text: A healer's house with a brass bell by the door and an inn with stew and early drinkers both stand open in a side lane of Alderwatch; Alaric must choose which to enter for his wounds.

thread.t27.1.text: Alaric owes healer Maren twenty silver for his bandaging, due within a day or two of his Guild payout
thread.t27.1.resolution: Maren's note declares them square unless the wound reopens or the shivering returns; she asks him to pay it forward to somebody bleeding on a road

thread.t32.1.text: Two adventurers at the Guild hall are talking about timber carts and the Millbrook road — possibly interested in the goblin snare-camp contract

thread.t47.1.text: Fresh tracks of a sixth goblin — small bare feet, a dragging left heel — lead east down the cut toward the timber road; it fled not long ago

thread.t50.1.text: Maren's fever warning has come true: the wound is hot and the shivering grips Alaric in waves at the healer's house; if the tea and draught fail by morning she sends for the temple
thread.t50.1.resolution: The night's fever broke; by morning the shivering did not return and the wound aches only dully under the bandage.

thread.t56.1.text: The Hartswell timber outfit will pay freelancers off the board to clear the goblin snare-camp if it is not cleared by tomorrow

thread.t57.1.text: A single line of small bare-foot tracks, one drag-toed, leads from the empty camp up the slope toward the dense pine stand atop the road-cut — the sixth goblin walked out.
thread.t57.1.resolution: the tracks ended at the wounded goblin under the overhang

thread.t61.1.text: The clerk notes folk in Alderwatch pay for a mage's work privately, off the board — no Guild credit and no Guild protection if it goes sour

thread.t65.1.text: The warden's office pays a bounty by the ear for goblin ear-tokens, separate from Guild contracts; the broker will take them if a contract doesn't want them

thread.t74.1.text: A wide splayed print in the mud downstream, filling slowly with returning water — evidence of some unseen creature.

thread.t75.1.text: A second, broader goblin emerged from the drain arch past full dark, carrying a lumpy skin; it paused at the dead one, mouth opening to chatter, as Alaric leveled his staff at its mouth
thread.t75.1.resolution: The goblin emerged and closed to melee; the encounter is now live combat.

thread.t78.1.text: The unseen heavier thing in the arch wandered near the light once, then dragged farther down into the deep; the fourth gutter goblin still lives somewhere in the dark drain.
thread.t78.1.resolution: the drag-sound's source emerged under the arch lip — a heavier, older gutter goblin hauling the third goblin's body back into the dark

thread.t102.1.text: The scarred bitch has backed off from the den toward the track at the base of the wall, watching the crest;
thread.t102.1.resolution: she was struck down by Alaric's bolt in the track's mouth and lies dead there

thread.t109.1.text: The pale bundle on the causeway tree is no pack: a torn coat, one laced boot and a satchel, the strap already in a rotvine tendril's grip; a shadow wider than the tendril rests in the dark water benea

thread.t111.1.text: The quiet dimples ended: the tendrils among the apple trees now stand at attention, tips pointed toward the shrine porch after the bell

thread.t112.1.text: A shrine lamp with a fresh ring-and-wave sigil was carried or lost by the tendrils right along the porch — evidence bearing on the missing shrine-keeper 'M'

thread.t113.1.text: The broad pale back lay in the flooded rows a long moment, then sank without hurry and did not come on toward the island once the tendrils were dead and the orchard silent.

thread.t116.1.text: The north corner's quiet has taken on a quality of attention, like a field under a hawk — whatever turned beneath the surface there is still keeping to its depth

thread.t120.1.text: The fifth rotvine tendril remains unseen — under the water, deeper in the rows, or gone altogether; the broad pale back did not resurface during the search
thread.t120.1.resolution: Alaric's search revealed it coiled beneath a fresh slick of broken stems, hiding or bracing, not yet dead.

thread.t134.1.text: Twice more something small went ticking away into the dark off to the left, quick and dry; the lamp caught only the tail-end of motion and settling dust

thread.t138.1.text: The whole field of dimples slid inward at once, and the three near the pillars drew toward the chest in a slow straight line.

thread.t140.1.text: The big thing beneath the black water rose partway at the chest, shoved a trough-shaped wake across the flooded chamber, but went no farther than the sill; the water's tongue crept two steps down and

thread.t146.1.text: A faint smell of long-cold char rises from below the grate, under the deep wet and old stone

thread.t152.1.text: The gutter-hound den under the collapsed mound shows no sign of the pack from the southern lip — whether they sleep below or range elsewhere, the field will not tell from a distance
thread.t152.1.resolution: Three hounds emerged from the den mouth as the light failed

thread.t156.1.text: The yammering under the den mound rose and fell — at least two throats, sometimes three — then stopped altogether; the den mouth sat silent and black, nothing came out.
thread.t156.1.resolution: Both remaining hounds accounted for: the big one killed, the lighter one fled deep and gone

thread.t158.1.text: The old woman in Ashenwell has yarrow salve and is dressing Alaric's hound bite by her fire
thread.t158.1.resolution: she finished the dressing herself and asked only pay what he thinks it's worth

thread.t160.1.text: Maud the healer wants Alaric to return in three days for her to check the hound bite on his arm

thread.t161.1.text: After the den-mouth hound dropped, a body hauled itself deeper into the mound — claws scrabbling lower in the dark, then quiet. Whatever remains of the pack is deeper down in the collapsed barrow den.
thread.t161.1.resolution: The quieter hound poured itself down a deeper crack of the barrow and vanished; the pack is ended

thread.t163.1.text: The big hound's deep bark carried across the barrow field and drew or held a fourth hound on the far ridge, watching the den — the pack may gather.

thread.t169.1.text: The deep growl resolved: the big hound is cornered ahead-right of the tunnel mouth, waiting, its breathing hitching as if deciding
thread.t169.1.resolution: Killed by Alaric's Arcane Bolt; dead at the slab's foot

thread.t188.1.text: The carrion ghoul gone to ground in the flooded south cut stays unseen from the lip; the water is deep enough to hide a dozen, with drowned machinery and a possible drowned gallery below.
thread.t188.1.resolution: Alaric shot it from behind the jut as it surfaced; the pale shape lies still an arm's length from the jut.

thread.t189.1.text: The dragging shape behind the standing wall found: a second carrion ghoul feeding at an intact stone cart at the shaded north end of the cut, with a third motionless shape deeper in the overhang's bla
thread.t189.1.resolution: the feeding ghoul was shot in the back and fell dead by the stone cart

thread.t220.1.text: A thin line of smoke rises from the direction of a reed-cutters' camp down the flats beyond the eel-weirs — the first sign of living people since dawn

thread.t221.1.text: The last bog strider keeps to the deeper reed beds by day and feeds toward evening; it was seen heading north by the black weir, and Marta's boy went after it hours ago
thread.t221.1.resolution: Alaric's search of the still water above the dam revealed the strider's wake and then the creature itself.

thread.t222.1.text: Something heavy slipped off a hummock into water ahead of Alaric on the walk north and vanished without showing itself

actions: 1. GOES — to eel-weirs of the Reed Flats (the story decides whether and where he arrives). Carry the way forward in this reply until he arrives, something acts on him, or a real choice of way appears; a sound, a shadow or a track without consequence is passed in a clause, never a stop.

resolutions.quote: I head back south across the flats toward the eel-weirs, keeping an eye out for whatever slipped into the water on my way north.

last.input: I head back south across the flats toward the eel-weirs, keeping an eye out for whatever slipped into the water on my way north.

inputs.input: I stay downwind and cast Arcane Bolt at the feeding bog strider.
I move along the hummocks toward the strider, keeping low in the reeds; once I'm within range, I cast Arcane Bolt at it.
I collect the feathers and talons from the strider's carcass, then move on north along the reed beds, searching for the next bog strider.
I stay still in the reeds, downwind, and cast Arcane Bolt at the second bog strider at forty paces.
I move along the reed line on my bank, closing to MEDIUM range, then cast Arcane Bolt at Bog Strider B.
I collect the feathers and talons from the second strider's carcass, then push on north along the reed beds, searching for the third bog strider.
I swing back east toward the open flats by the eel-weirs, searching there for the third bog strider.
I walk down to the reed-cutters' camp and ask whether anyone there has seen a bog strider moving today, and where.
I thank them, tell them two striders are already down and the boats should launch again soon, then head north toward the black weir to hunt the third one there.
I walk out onto the black weir's platform, testing the boards as I go, and search the still water above the dam for the third bog strider.
I move along the dam's spine to close to MEDIUM range, then cast Arcane Bolt at Bog Strider C.
I head back south across the flats toward the eel-weirs, keeping an eye out for whatever slipped into the water on my way north.

The way back was slower in the failing light. He kept off the deepest channels where he could, and he kept watching the water — every dark hummock shadow, every slow swirl of current, read twice before he trusted it.

Whatever had slipped off that hummock on his way north gave him only one sign of itself. Crossing the same ground near the third marker, he caught a broad ripple spreading out from a reed clump some twenty paces east, and beneath it, for half a breath, the low dark line of a back moving away through the shallows — big, unhurried, going from him, not toward. It was gone between one step and the next, and the reeds stood still again. He gave that clump its distance and walked on.

The light was nearly gone from the sky when the eel-weirs came back around him, the stakes of them standing black out of the darkening water. The campfires were lit on the hummock island. He could smell fish and reed smoke, and hear the binding men at their work, and from the channel by the largest weir came the sound of poles and water — the boats out again, as promised, lanterns swinging low over the eel baskets. Figures worked the weirs in the last light, and one of the boats putted its way toward the reed-cutters' channel, the day's work finally moving.

The flats were quiet around him. Four striders down, the cull done, and the walk back out of the Reed Flats ahead of him in the dark.
